dataIdInfo.idPurp:
Part of the Elections NWT mandate is to provide maps to all the Deputy Returning Officers and for candidate use during the periodic NWT Elections. To create these maps requires accurate boundaries of each of the Electoral Districts of the NWT. This is a 2023 update based on the 2012 Electoral Boundary Commission of the boundaries created for the 2011 Territorial Election.
The dataset is a compilation of the boundaries of the 19 NWT Electoral Districts based upon the 2012 Electoral Boundary Commission and the legal descriptions found in Bill 18 of Fifth Session, Seventeenth Legislative Assembly plus any Polling Divisions within each Electoral District as determined by Elections NWT. This is the Electoral Districts dataset.
There have been changes from the 2011 data, with Inuvik Boot Lake and Twin Lakes, Hay River North and South, Tu Nedhé - Wiilideh, Great Slave, Frame Lake, Kam Lake, Range Lake, Yellowknife Centre, Yellowknife South and Yellowknife North Electoral Districts all being updated.
Added a 'Electoral Year' field in 2023, to both Electoral Districts and Polling Divisions to identity the differences starting from 2015.
dataIdInfo.idAbs:
Part of the Elections NWT mandate is to provide maps to all the Deputy Returning Officers and for candidate use during the periodic NWT Elections. To create these maps requires accurate boundaries of each of the Electoral Districts of the NWT. This is an update from the boundaries created for the 2011 Territorial Election based on the 2012 Electoral Boundary Commission.

In 2009, using Schedule A from the Legislative Assembly and Executive Council Act of the GNWT, the legal descriptions were used to create the original Electoral Districts. The existing legal descriptions were reviewed and issues were detailed in the supplemental information. The Chief Electoral Officer did not believe that these would affect any potential voters so they were addressed as part of the Electoral Boundary Commission.

Draft boundaries were created for each Scenario based on Stats Canada Dissemination Block and population data to create the population balance per Electoral District. Once this balance was created, the actual draft boundaries were adjusted as required.

These draft boundaries were then used to create legal descriptions of the 19 Electoral Districts as described in Bill 18 of Fifth Session, Seventeenth Legislative Assembly.

A revision to the Nunakput boundary was also included to reflect the change in what is now considered to be the western boundary of Canada in the Northwest Territories.

The revision included the use of the NRCan Canadian Geopolitical Boundaries (CGB1) as a framework outline of the NWT. While the final boundary closely matches this boundaries there are a few locations were the NWT boundary does not match. At the scale that this data will be used, it was determined that this is acceptable.

As part of the Electoral District Map updates for the 2015 Territorial Elections a final version of the revised boundaries were created.

dataIdInfo.suppInfo:
The 2009 legal descriptions were reviewed as part of the boundary creation and ‘problem’ areas were identified with recommended solutions.
• some places where there appear to be typos • within some of the Yellowknife Electoral Districts there have been some changes in Lot, Block and Plan designations as a result of new surveys being completed and the original Lot references are no longer valid • In some spots, the description could be simplified without affecting the intent of the boundaries
There were some additional specific concerns: • The northern limits of Nunakput do not follow any accepted NWT boundary. • Hay River South appears to use the Enterprise Community Boundary northern extent as its southern boundary • Only YK Centre of the Yellowknife EDs does not include part of the Yellowknife Municipal Boundary as part of it • Fort Smith is on the 60th parallel and portions of it according to survey monuments are actually in Alberta • Kam Lake ED, the NW boundary with YK South was based on a parcel that has now been resurveyed and the legal description would have it cross several parcels that were created as part of this split. It was noted that there are no residences that are affected at this time so the adjustment will be made after the Election.
The Chief Electoral Officer, David Brock stated that he did not think that the problem areas would affect any voters so these will be addressed after the election.
2014 Bill 18:
* does have a few typos * there have been some surveying done since the legal descriptions were written in 2013 and potentially the legal descriptions should be updated. * Nunakput bounday has been updated to reflect the generally accepted western boundary of Canada in the NWT. * The Yellowknife and Hay RIver Municipal boundary legal descriptions were used to generate the outer limites of the applicable Electoral Districts. * there were two small changes that affected the boundaries of Kam Lake and Yellowknife South that are not reflected in the Boundary Commission Report. (excerpt from email sent by David Brock, 02 December 2014:
Instructions re: boundary between Kam Lake and Yellowknife South (S19)
After making all other adjustments to the Kam Lake / YK South boundary proposed by the EBC in their Final Report, move the block of dwellings inside Larocque Crescent and Bourque Drive (DB 14303) as well as the block of dwellings inside Lamoureax Road and Hordal Road (DB 14202) from Yellowknife South to Kam Lake. [Census: 138 persons; 59 + 79, respectively.]
Revised Population Estimates Yellowknife South -- 2784 (+ 22.0 %) Kam Lake – 2810 (+ 23.1 %)
This brings both ridings under + 25 % variance.

dataLineage.statement:
Part of the Elections NWT mandate is to provide maps to all the Deputy Returning Officers and for candidate use during the periodic NWT Elections. To create these maps requires accurate boundaries of each of the Electoral Districts of the NWT. This is a 2015 update based on the 2012 Electoral Boundary Commission of the boundaries created for the 2011 Teritorial Election .
This dataset will be updated as required to meet the needs of Elections NWT.

prcStep.stepDesc: Added electoral year field to enable keeping historic data and differentiating between different election year boundaries. Electoral boundaries emained the same but small update to polling divisions for 2023 election year.

Starting in late 2009, Schedule A from the Legislative Assembly and Executive Council Act of the GNWT, the legal descriptions were used to create each Electoral District.
For the actual creation of each ED, existing digital data was used and included the following: • MACA (now ATLAS) data for lot, block and plan data for parcels, hydrology data within urban areas. These were saved on an ED basis • National Road Network data for centre lines of roads within urban areas. These were saved on an ED basis • Inuvialuit western and northern boundaries will be used to close off the outer limits of Nunakput • NWT boundary created by the GNWT NWTCG for most of NWT boundary • NRCan CGB1 provincial polygon data for Nunavut boundary to southern limits of Nunakput and Yukon boundary to reduce edits • Mackenzie Delta and Tu Nedhe shapefiles from previous projects.
Digital data that had to be created: • ED straight line segments using Excel, text files and GENERATE • 20 mile buffer of the Beaufort Sea for Nunakput boundary using 1:250,000 NTDB data and the BUFFER command.
Once all data created, it was compiled using APPEND with NOTEST. To close all polygons within the shapefile using ArcMap was not possible so used ARC/INFO Workstation.
Attributes included the Electoral District Name and wither or not the Electoral District was in Yellowknife.
Boundary was complete as of end of 2010.
prcStep.stepRat: It was necessary to use a number of data sources to compile the data into the final Electoral District boundaries

prcStep.stepDesc: In August 2011, the decision was made to create digital Polling Division data. These boundaries were based on a document: 2011 Polling Divisions_Descriptions and Keys_24 June 2011.docx provided by Elections NWT. The polling division descriptions were created by each Electoral District and were not consistent or clear. The Chief Electoral Officer had to make interpretations on some boundary locations. This dataset only included an areal layer and a linear layer. No attributes were ever included nor was the data ever finalized. Labelling on maps was text based and not attribute based.
prcStep.stepRat: Primary project lead was on annual and was not able to get final project work details from summer student. These data layers will not be part of the current dataset.

prcStep.stepDesc:
An Electoral Boundary Commission was established in 2012 to review existing Electoral Districts and develop Scenarios for 18, 19 and 21 Electoral Districts.
The Boundary Commission had the objective to balance the population/electoral district to be within +/- 25% of the territorial average population/Electoral District for each Scenario. Draft boundaries were created for each Scenario based on Stats Canada Dissemination Block and population data to create the population balance per Electoral District. Once this balance was created, the draft actual boundaries were adjusted as required for reporting purposes.
The decision was made not to finalize each scenario boundaries, but wait until the Legislative Assembly made a determination of the final number of Electoral Districts.
These draft boundaries were then used to create legal descriptions for 19 Electoral Districts as descibed in Bill 18 of Fifth Session, Seventeenth Legislative Assembly. Legal descriptions were also drafted for the 21 Electoral Districts Scenario as it was determined that there may be a legal challenge on the 19 District Scenario.
A revision was made to the Nunakput western boundary to reflect the change in what is now considered to be the western boundary of Canada in the Northwest Territories.

In preparation for the 2015 NWT Territorial Election, changes to the 19 existing Electoral Districts based on the 19 Electoral District Scenario from to the 2012 boundary commission were made. These included changes to Inuvik Boot and Twin Lakes, Hay River North and South, Tu Nedhé - Wiilideh, Great Slave, Frame Lake, Kam Lake, Range Lake, Yellowknife Centre, Yellowknife South, Yellowknife North and Nunakput Electoral Districts.
The revision included the use of the NRCan Canadian Geopolitical Boundaries (CGB1) as a framework outline of the NWT. While the final boundary closely matches this boundaries there are a few locations were the NWT boundary does not match. At the scale that this data will be used, it was determined that this is acceptable.

The revised Electoral Districts were used in consultation with the Deputy Returning Officers for Elections NWT to revise any required Polling Division boundaries.
The revised Electoral District data layer was used as the frame for the Polling Division data layer.
With the Electoral Districts and Polling Divisions being used in a web-mapping application, it was also necessary to determine the 'rural extents' of any Polling District. These were developed using natural features and logical travel routes where possible.
Attributes have also been added for Polling Division Number and Name.

The development of the Polling Divisions data found minor edits required to the Electoral Districts Data. The Dissolve Command with the EDName Attribute was used with the Polling Divisions data to recreate the Electoral Districts Data.
